title: Your key to the fleet
briefing: Welcome to ops-01, the jump host you'll use to reach other servers over ssh.
Before logging into anything, set up an SSH key pair: a private key you keep
secret and a public key you hand to servers. Then you log in with no password.
tips: `ssh-keygen -t ed25519` makes a modern key in ~/.ssh.
It writes two files: id_ed25519 (private, mode 600) and id_ed25519.pub (public).
objective: Generate an ed25519 SSH key pair in ~/.ssh (a private key and its .pub).
expert_objective: Create an ed25519 key pair under ~/.ssh.
hints: Run `ssh-keygen -t ed25519` and accept the default location.
`ssh-keygen -t ed25519` — then `ls -l ~/.ssh` shows both files (private key is 600).
explanation: Key-based auth is how real ssh works: the private key never leaves your machine (that's why it's mode 600), and the matching .pub goes on the servers you log into. No passwords flying over the network — just proof you hold the private key.
